# app/controllers/api/webhooks_controller.rb
class Api::WebhooksController < ApplicationController
  skip_before_action :verify_authenticity_token
  before_action :validate_callback_url, only: [:register]

  # POST /api/webhooks/register
  # Registers a webhook callback URL for event notifications
  def register
    url = params[:callback_url]
    
    # Resolve the hostname to check it's not internal
    resolved = resolve_host(URI.parse(url).host)
    
    if internal_ip?(resolved)
      render json: { error: 'Internal addresses not allowed' }, status: :forbidden
      return
    end

    # Store webhook registration
    webhook = Webhook.new(
      callback_url: url,
      user_id: current_user.id,
      secret: SecureRandom.hex(32),
      events: params[:events] || ['all']
    )

    if webhook.save
      # Verify the webhook endpoint is reachable by sending a challenge
      verify_endpoint(webhook)
      render json: { id: webhook.id, secret: webhook.secret }, status: :created
    else
      render json: { errors: webhook.errors.full_messages }, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  end

  # POST /api/webhooks/:id/test
  # Sends a test event to the registered webhook
  def test
    webhook = current_user.webhooks.find(params[:id])
    deliver_event(webhook, { event: 'test', timestamp: Time.current.iso8601 })
    render json: { status: 'delivered' }
  end

  private

  def resolve_host(hostname)
    Resolv.getaddress(hostname)
  end

  def internal_ip?(ip)
    addr = IPAddr.new(ip)
    [
      IPAddr.new('10.0.0.0/8'),
      IPAddr.new('172.16.0.0/12'),
      IPAddr.new('192.168.0.0/16'),
      IPAddr.new('127.0.0.0/8'),
      IPAddr.new('169.254.0.0/16'),
      IPAddr.new('::1/128'),
      IPAddr.new('fc00::/7')
    ].any? { |range| range.include?(addr) }
  end

  def verify_endpoint(webhook)
    challenge = SecureRandom.hex(16)
    uri = URI.parse(webhook.callback_url)
    
    # TOCTOU: DNS is resolved again here, after the check above
    # An attacker can use DNS rebinding to point to internal services
    http = Net::HTTP.new(uri.host, uri.port)
    http.use_ssl = (uri.scheme == 'https')
    http.open_timeout = 5
    http.read_timeout = 10
    
    request = Net::HTTP::Post.new(uri.path.presence || '/')
    request['Content-Type'] = 'application/json'
    request['X-Webhook-Challenge'] = challenge
    request.body = { challenge: challenge }.to_json

    response = http.request(request)
    
    # Cache the response for debugging
    cache_file = Rails.root.join('tmp', 'webhook_verifications', "#{webhook.id}.json")
    FileUtils.mkdir_p(File.dirname(cache_file))
    File.write(cache_file, {
      status: response.code,
      body: response.body.truncate(4096),
      headers: response.each_header.to_h,
      verified_at: Time.current.iso8601
    }.to_json)

    webhook.update(verified: response.code == '200')
  rescue StandardError => e
    Rails.logger.warn("Webhook verification failed: #{e.message}")
    webhook.update(verified: false)
  end

  def deliver_event(webhook, payload)
    uri = URI.parse(webhook.callback_url)
    http = Net::HTTP.new(uri.host, uri.port)
    http.use_ssl = (uri.scheme == 'https')
    http.open_timeout = 5
    http.read_timeout = 10

    request = Net::HTTP::Post.new(uri.path.presence || '/')
    request['Content-Type'] = 'application/json'
    request['X-Webhook-Signature'] = OpenSSL::HMAC.hexdigest('SHA256', webhook.secret, payload.to_json)
    request.body = payload.to_json

    http.request(request)
  end

  def validate_callback_url
    url = params[:callback_url]
    unless url.present? && url.match?(/\Ahttps?:\/\//)
      render json: { error: 'Invalid callback URL' }, status: :bad_request
    end
  end
end

environment.description: Same Rails 7.1 application deployed on hardened Kubernetes pod with the following runtime constraints: container rootfs mounted read-only (readOnlyRootFilesystem: true in securityContext), no emptyDir or tmpfs volumes mounted at any path including /tmp or Rails.root/tmp. Pod uses a distroless Ruby base image. The container's resolv.conf points to a CoreDNS instance with the 'loop' and 'bufsize' plugins but notably does NOT have any DNS filtering policy plugin enabled. Network egress is controlled by a Cilium L3/L4 NetworkPolicy that allows TCP/443 outbound to 0.0.0.0/0 CIDR but the policy's entitySelector excludes 'world' for non-TLS ports. Pod runs with seccomp profile RuntimeDefault.

config.volumes: none (no emptyDir, no tmpfs, no PVC mounted at tmp paths)
config.dns: CoreDNS with loop and bufsize plugins, no filtering
config.network_policy: Cilium L3/L4: egress TCP/443 to 0.0.0.0/0, no other ports allowed outbound
